relations.subject: search:date-time-parser
relations.evidence: The dateTimeOptional date/time parser uses 6 layouts, in [percentStyle](date-time-parser-layout-styles.md#percent) format, to parse date and time strings.

relations.subject: search:date-time-parser
relations.evidence: Set the default date/time parser for your Search index from the Server Web Console's' [Advanced Settings](set-advanced-settings.md) or your [JSON Search index definition](search-index-params.md#default-date-time-parser).

relations.subject: search:date-time-parser
relations.evidence: You can also set a date/time parser when using [Date Range facets](search-request-params.md#date) or a [date range query](search-request-params.md#date-range-queries).

relations.subject: search:full-text-index
relations.evidence: Use a date/time parser to tell the Search Service how to interpret date and time data in your documents.

notable_absence.finding: Unlike tokenizers and token filters, this component DOES have a documented default: search-index-params.md states default_datetime_parser's value is 'dateTimeOptional' in its example payload. This page itself, however, never states that dateTimeOptional is the default - a reader landing on this page alone would not learn which parser applies by default; that fact only surfaces on the separate search-index-params.md page.
